μυσ.def: μῦς I. Lat. mus, a mouse, Batr.; μ. ἀρουραῖος the field-mouse, or the hamster, Hdt.; μῦς πίσσας γεύεται, proverb. of one who is tempted to eat and finds himself caught, Theocr. II. a muscle of the body, Lat. musculus, id.

μυσαροσ.def: μῠσᾰρός, ή, όν (μύσος) 1. foul, dirty: hence, loathsome, abominable, Eur.; τὸ μ. an abomination, Hdt. 2. of persons, defiled, polluted, Eur.

μυσαττομαι.def: μῠσάττομαι, (μύσος) Dep.: to feel disgust at anything loathsome, to loathe, abominate, c. acc., Eur., Xen.

μυσαχθησ.def: μῠσαχθής, ές (from μῠσάττομαι) (poetic for μυσαρός, Anth.)

μυσιοσ.def: Μῡ́σιος, η, ον (Μυσός) a Mysian dirge, Aesch.; cf. Κίσσιος.

μυσοσ.def: μῠ́σος, εος, τό, uncleanness of body or mind: metaph. an abomination, defilement, Lat. piaculum, Trag.
Μῡσός, οῦ, ὁ, a Mysian, Aesch.:—from their effeminate character, Μυσῶν λεία came to mean a prey to all, of anything that can be plundered with impunity, Dem.

μυσπολεω.gloss: to run about like a mouse
μυσπολεω.def: μυς-πολέω, (μῦς) to run about like a mouse, Ar.

μυσταγωγια.def: μυστᾰγωγία, ἡ, initiation into the mysteries, Plut.

μυσταγωγοσ.gloss: one who initiates into mysteries, a mystagogue
μυσταγωγοσ.def: μυστ-ᾰγωγός, οῦ, ὁ, (μύστης, ἄγω) one who initiates into mysteries, a mystagogue, Plut.

μυσταξ.def: μύσταξ, ακος, doric and Lacon. word, the upper lip, the moustache, Theocr.: cf. μάσταξ.

μυστηρικοσ.def: μυστηρικός, ή, όν of or for mysteries, mystic, Ar.

μυστηριον.def: μυστήριον, ου, τό, (μύστης) 1. a mystery or secret doctrine; in pl., τὰ μ. the mysteries of the Cabiri in Samothrace, Hdt.; of Demeter at Eleusis, Aesch., etc. 2. any mystery or secret, Plat. 3. mystic implements, Eur., Ar. 4. in NTest. a mystery, a divine secret, something above human intelligence.

μυστηρισ.def: μυστηρίς, ίδος, (pecul. fem. of μυστηρικός, Anth.)

μυστηριωτισ.def: μυστηριῶτις, ιδος, ἡ, (μυστήριον) of or for the mysteries: μ. σπονδή an armistice during the Eleusinian mysteries, Aeschin.

μυστησ.def: μύστης, ου, ὁ, (μυέω) 1. one initiated, Eur. 2. as adj. mystic, Ar., Anth.

μυστικοσ.def: μυστικός, ή, όν (from μύστης) mystic, connected with the mysteries, μ. Ἴακχος the mystic chant Iacchus, Hdt.; τὰ μ. the mysteries, Thuc.:— χοιρία μ., in Ar., are prob. wretched lean pigs, such as the μύσται were wont to offer.

μυστιλαομαι.def: μυστῑλάομαι, Dep. to sop bread in soup or gravy and eat it, Ar.: metaph., μυστιλᾶται τῶν δημοσίων he ladles out public money, id.:—perf. part. in pass. sense, scooped out, id. (from μυστῑ́λη)

μυστιλη.def: μυστῑ́λη, ἡ, a piece of bread used to sup up soup or gravy with, Ar. (deriv. uncertain)

μυστιπολοσ.def: μυστῐ-πόλος, ον (μύστης, πολέω) solemnising mysteries, performing mystic rites, Anth.

μυστισ.def: μύστις (fem. of μύστης) I. as adj. mystic, Anth. II. a mystagogue, Anacreont.

μυστοδοκοσ.def: μυστο-δόκος, ον (μύστης, δέχομαι) receiving the initiated, δόμος μ., i. e. Eleusis, Ar.

μυτιληνη.def: Μῠτῐλήνη, ἡ, Mytilene, the chief city of Lesbos, Thuc.

μυττωτευω.gloss: to hash up, make mince-meat of
μυττωτευω.def: μυττωτεύω, to hash up, make mince-meat of, τινά Ar.

μυττωτοσ.gloss: a savoury dish of cheese, honey, garlic
μυττωτοσ.def: μυττωτός, οῦ, ὁ, a savoury dish of cheese, honey, garlic, mashed up into a sort of paste, Lat. moretum, Ar. (deriv. uncertain)

μυχθισμοσ.def: μυχθισμός, οῦ, ὁ, a snorting, moaning, Eur.

μυχιοσ.def: μύχιος, η, ον (μῠχός) inward, inmost, retired, embayed, Aesch., Luc.

μυχμοσ.def: μυχμός, οῦ, ὁ, (μύζω) = μυγμός moaning, groaning, Od.

μυχοθεν.gloss: from the inmost part of the house, from the women's chambers
μυχοθεν.def: μυχόθεν (μυχός) adv. from the inmost part of the house, from the women's chambers, Aesch.

μυχοιτατοσ.def: μῠχοίτατος, η, ον (irreg. Sup. of μύχιος) in the farthest corner, Od.

μυχονδε.def: μυχόνδε (μυχός) adv. to the far corner, Od.

μυχοσ.def: μῠχός, οῦ, ὁ, (μύω) 1. the innermost place, inmost nook or corner, Lat. sinus, recessus, Hom., etc. 2. the inmost part of a house, the women's apartments, Lat. penetralia, Od., Trag. 3. a bay or creek running far inland, Hdt.; πόντιος μ., i. e. the Adriatic, Aesch.

μυχωδησ.def: μῠχ-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) full of recesses, cavernous, Eur.

μυω.def: μύω I. intr. to close, be shut, of the eyes, Il., Eur.; so, χείλεα μεμυκώς having the lips closed, Anth. 2. of persons, μύσας with one's eyes shut, Soph., Ar. 3. metaph. to be lulled to rest, to abate, of pain, Soph.; of storms, Anth. II. trans. to close, shut, id.

μυων.gloss: a cluster of muscles, a muscle
μυων.def: μῡών, ῶνος, ὁ, (μῦς II) a cluster of muscles, a muscle, Il.

μυωπαζω.def: μυωπάζω, (μύωψ) to be shortsighted, see dimly, NTest.

μυωπιζω.gloss: to spur, prick with a spur
μυωπιζω.def: μυωπίζω, (μύωψ II. 2) I. to spur, prick with a spur, Xen. II. Pass. (μύωψ II. 1) to be teased by flies, of a horse, id.

μυωψ.def: μύ-ωφαιλινγ ον λεμβυφ [] (μύω, ὤψ) I. contracting the eyes, as shortsighted people do, shortsighted, Arist. II. as Subst., the horsefly or gadfly, Lat. tabanus, Aesch., Plat. 2. a good, spur, Xen., Theophr.:—metaph. a stimulant, Luc., Anth.

μωλοσ.def: μῶλος, ὁ, the toil and moil of war, Il.; ξείνου καὶ Ἴρου μ. the struggle between Irus and the stranger, Od.

μωλυ.def: μῶλυ moly, mandrake, a fabulous herb of magic power, having a black root and white blossom, given by Hermes to Ulysses, as a counter-charm to the charms of Circe, Od.

μωμαομαι.def: μωμάομαι, (μῶμος) Dep.: to find, fault with, blame, c. acc., Il., Aesch.:—an aor1 inf. μωμηθῆναι in pass. sense, NTest.

μωμητοσ.def: μωμητός, ή, όν (μωμάομαι) to be blamed, Aesch.

μωμοσ.def: μῶμος, ὁ, I. blame, ridicule, disgrace, μῶμον ἀνάψαι to set a brand upon one, Od. II. personified Momus, the critic God, Hes. (Akin to μέμφομαι?)

μων.gloss: but surely not? is it so?
μων.def: μῶν contr. for μὴ οὖν, used like μή, in questions to which a negative answer is expected, but surely not? is it so? Lat. num? μῶν ἐστι..; Answ. οὐ δῆτα, Eur.: sometimes it asks doubtingly like Lat. num forte? and answered in the affirm., id.: — μῶν οὐ..; requires an affirm. answer, Lat. nonne ? Trag.

μωνυξ.def: μῶ-νυξ, υχος, (μόνος, ὄνυξ) with a single, i. e. uncloven, hoof, Lat. solipes, of the horse, Hom., Eur.

μωραινω.def: μωραίνω, (μῶρος) I. to be silly, foolish, Eur., Xen., etc.:—c. acc. rei, πεῖραν μωραίνειν to make a mad attempt, Aesch. II. Causal, to make foolish, convict of folly, NTest.:—Pass., of salt, to become insipid, lose its savour, id.

μωρια.def: μωρία, ἡ, (μῶρος) silliness, folly, μωρίην ἐπιφέρειν τινι to impute folly to him, Hdt.; μωρίαν ὀφλισκάνειν to be charged with it, Soph.; ἐδόκει μωρία εἶναι ταῦτα Thuc.; τῆς μωρίας! what folly! Ar.

μωρολογια.def: μωρολογία, ἡ, silly talking, NTest. (from μωρολόγος)

μωροσ.def: μωρός, ή, όν dull, sluggish, stupid, Soph., etc.; τὸ- μ. folly, Eur.; μῶρα φρονεῖν, δρᾶν, λέγειν Soph., Eur.:—adv. -ρως, Xen.

μωροσοφοσ.def: μωρό-σοφος, ον foolishly wise, a sapient fool, Luc.
